title: fix(ui): reduce background traffic when opening chats
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Opening a chat downloads full automation definitions just to populate the sidebar Inbox badge, including prompts and commands the badge never uses.

## User Impact

Inbox transfers substantially less data while preserving failed, overdue, running, and automatically disabled job handling. Automation editing, access checks, pagination, and dismissal behavior stay intact. No configuration changes or production data migration are required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Inbox now uses the existing compact automation inventory, with the four facts its alerts need: agent identity, update time, active-run time, and automatic-disable status. Full and compact readers share pagination and snapshot recovery; the automation editor retains complete definitions. The automation tool output schema accepts these facts while preserving older compact and full inventory responses.

The browser fixtures return the correct inventory shape. The plugin settings test verifies that Save submits the current hash and edited configuration; the mock configuration regression preserves acknowledged snapshots across immediate reload, including distinct applied hashes and continued revisions. The mention-flow test waits for its own filtered refresh instead of inspecting the last session-list request across independent consumers. SQLite test teardown now awaits database shutdown.

The disclosure focus ring also gains permanent horizontal padding so it does not crowd the label.

## Evidence

The registered browser flow with 55 synthetic jobs receives **17,794 JSON response bytes instead of 403,177 bytes (95.6% less)** across the same two pages, with the same three alerts. The original implementation fails both the browser payload assertion and the Gateway compact-alert regression. This establishes synthetic payload reduction, not live chat latency or compressed network bytes.

Focused proof covers 266 Gateway tests, 357 UI tests, and 220 automation output-contract tests, including actual Code Mode execution and older compact/full replies. The runtime revision passed 28 browser scenarios across compact Inbox inventory, message actions, tool outcomes, and plugin settings ownership. The mention-flow repair passes all three relevant browser cases and the roster-versus-child request helper test; CI supplied the original cross-query failure.

An earlier published head passed all hosted CI. After resolving the mock-fixture conflict against current main, the consolidated mock boundary suite passes all 16 tests. All four current-head compact Inbox and plugin-settings browser cases pass, and independent P0–P2 review has no actionable findings. Selected changed checks, including core/UI types, lint, and dead exports, pass. CI subsequently exposed a wall-clock race in an existing sidebar pagination test. Its event phase now advances the actual 200 ms debounce with a fake clock, preserving the one-request, 400-row, and exact page-size assertions. All 471 sidebar cases pass before and after the change; targeted lint/formatting and fresh independent review pass. Exact-head hosted CI passed on `d2f08f001cec5779de5a6ca139ff5988c3c106cc`: 157 successful jobs and 13 skipped. The full check rollup is green. The existing before/after captures below still match the authored UI changes.
